title: Mimicry without understanding: the origins of decision bias in large language models
abstract: arXiv:2608.12339v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language models (LLMs) were found to be susceptible to a host of social, affective, and cognitive biases. We examined two mechanisms through which such biases can be generated even when human preferences (in the training data) are not biased or when they are correctly categorized as being biased. The first is faulty mimicry of preferences based on human behavior: this involves LLMs inferring human preferences even when behaviors are logically unrelated to preferences. The second is mimicry of explicitly biased human behaviors. In four studies focusing on economic biases, we find that ChatGPT-4o and Qwen exhibited social proof biases even when prompted with reports of human behaviors that were clearly non-indicative of individuals' actual preferences. translated_title: 无理解的模仿：大型语言模型中决策偏差的起源
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）被发现易受一系列社会、情感和认知偏差的影响。我们考察了两种机制，即使人类偏好（在训练数据中）不存在偏差，或者这些偏好被正确分类为有偏差时，这些偏差也可能被生成。第一种是对基于人类行为的偏好的错误模仿：这涉及LLMs即使行为在逻辑上与偏好无关，也会推断出人类偏好。第二种是对明确有偏差的人类行为的模仿。在四项聚焦于经济偏差的研究中，我们发现ChatGPT-4o和Qwen在收到明确不反映个体实际偏好的人类行为报告时，也表现出社会认同偏差。LLMs在明确描述为偏差的情况下也表现出损失厌恶。事实上，当提示详细科学报告时，LLMs中偏差（即损失厌恶）的程度与人类相当。
tldr: 本文揭示了大型语言模型即使在没有真实人类偏好或明确标注偏差的情况下，也可能通过错误模仿人类行为而产生决策偏差。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that large language models can generate decision biases through faulty mimicry of human behaviors, even when human preferences are unbiased or correctly labeled as biased.
